Abstract In cloud computing, scheduling workflows for data-intensive tasks is challenging due to task dependencies,  heterogeneous resources, and high computational demands, all of which affect cost, execution time, and energy  usage. This research proposes a novel hybrid optimization algorithm called Dolphin Swarm Sparrow Search  Optimization (DSSSO) to address these challenges. The DSSSO model combines the broad search capability of  Dolphin Swarm Optimization with the precise tuning ability of Sparrow Search Algorithm, enabling effective  exploration and exploitation in the solution space. Unlike existing scheduling models that primarily optimize  makespan and cost, the proposed DSSSO explicitly integrates energy consumption and resource utilization into  a unified multi-objective framework. This dual-phase design—leveraging dolphins for global exploration and  sparrows for local exploitation—ensures both convergence stability and adaptability in heterogeneous cloud  environments. The main objective is to minimize makespan, reduce energy consumption, and lower scheduling  cost while maximizing resource utilization. The model is evaluated using benchmark scientific workflows such as  CyberShake, Montage, Epigenomics, and LIGO. Simulation results show that DSSSO outperforms existing methods,  achieving up to 12% lower makespan, 15% less energy consumption, and 10% better resource usage compared to  algorithms like Hybrid Bat Optimization and Improved Bat Optimization. Keywords  Cloud computing, Workflow scheduling, Optimization algorithms, Dolphin swarm optimization, Sparrow  search algorithm

Moreover, the adaptation of  heterogenous cloud computing added to the challenges  and complexities in scientific workflow task scheduling.  When it comes to quality of service again large work­ flow scheduling should provide reliability, scalability and  resource utilization to users which makes this schedul­ ing process as NP-hard problem. Thus, it is essential to  introduce solutions which should provide better Quality  of Services (QoS) to users.
The research community provided a wide range of  solutions to manage and schedule the scientific workflow  applications. The existing researches considered user  defined QoS parameters in addition to communication  rates and processing capacity. However, the major chal­ lenge of workflow scheduling is present in minimizing  the cost, make span and energy consumption while accel­ erating the throughput. It is essential to consider these  multiple constraints while optimizing the resources.  Moreover, different workflow applications require vari­ ous strategies when they are adapted to heterogeneous  systems. The review presented in [3] provides a compre­ hensive summary of user tasks and workflow scheduling  techniques based on architectures. Another review pre­ sented in [4] summarizes different workflow applications  and scheduling techniques under different categories like  resource scheduling, energy efficient scheduling and fault  tolerant scheduling. Both review works summarizes that  optimization algorithms will be the best choice for sched­ uling scientific workflow applications.
Optimization algorithms are developed to provide opti­ mal solutions to real world optimization. The naturally  occurred events are formulated and created as optimiza­ tion algorithms. Heuristic, nature inspired, metaheuristic  and evolutionary optimization algorithms are developed  and utilized in various domains like image processing,  networking, signal processing, etc. Various optimization  algorithms are used for workflow applications [5, 6]. Dif­ ferent types of metaheuristic optimization algorithms  are studied in [7] for workflow scheduling and provided  a detailed comparative analysis which is quite useful to  summarize the limitations of conventional optimization  algorithm-based workflow scheduling. Another review  presented in [8] considered PSO algorithm and its merits  and demerits in scheduling in detail. Researchers devel­ oped workflow scheduling based on optimization algo­ rithms like genetic algorithm, bat optimization algorithm,  ant colony optimization [9–12], whale optimization [13].  However, the existing approaches mainly considered  make span and cost as their objective functions. It is  essential to consider other metrics like energy consump­ tion and resource utilization in objective functions to  provide better QoS to users. While previous studies have
explored various optimization-based workflow sched­ uling techniques, most focus primarily on minimizing  makespan and cost, often overlooking equally critical  factors such as energy consumption and resource utiliza­ tion. Moreover, many existing approaches struggle with  maintaining a balance between exploration and exploita­ tion during the optimization process, frequently resulting  in premature convergence and suboptimal task-resource  mappings. These limitations highlight a clear research  gap: the need for a robust, multi-objective schedul­ ing algorithm that can effectively address multiple QoS  constraints in heterogeneous cloud environments while  maintaining solution diversity and convergence stability.
To bridge this gap, this research introduces a novel  hybrid optimization algorithm—Dolphin Swarm Sparrow  Search Optimization (DSSSO)—that integrates the global  exploration capabilities of Dolphin Swarm Optimization  (DSO) with the local refinement efficiency of the Sparrow  Search Algorithm (SSA). This hybrid model is specifically  designed to optimize four critical objectives simultane­ ously: makespan, energy consumption, cost, and resource  utilization. By leveraging the complementary strengths of  DSO and SSA, the DSSSO algorithm offers a more adap­ tive and scalable solution for workflow scheduling com­ pared to conventional and hybrid metaheuristic models.
The proposed DSSSO framework stands out by  addressing multiple shortcomings in the literature: it  incorporates energy and resource-aware objectives often  ignored in prior work, employs a dual-phase optimiza­ tion to avoid local optima, and demonstrates superior  performance across diverse scientific workflows. This  clear enhancement over existing techniques establishes  the novelty and practical relevance of the research.
Most existing workflow scheduling approaches opti­ mize only one or two objectives, typically makespan and  cost, while critical aspects such as energy consumption  and resource utilization remain underexplored. More­ over, conventional optimization models frequently suffer  from premature convergence due to imbalance between  exploration and exploitation, leading to suboptimal task- to-resource mappings in heterogeneous cloud settings.  This leaves a clear research gap: the need for a unified,  multi-objective scheduling model that simultaneously  addresses makespan, cost, energy consumption, and  resource utilization, while ensuring convergence stabil­ ity and scalability in dynamic cloud environments. The  present work is motivated by this gap and introduces the  DSSSO framework as a robust solution.
Thus, a hybrid optimization is presented in this  research work as a multi-objective model which provides  optimal solution for workflow scheduling application.  The research work major contributions are summarized  as follows.

Related work Optimization algorithm used for workflow scheduling  are considered for research analysis. The existing meth­ odology and its features are studied in this section in  detail. The workflow scheduling model presented in [14]  allows scheduling based on dynamic task priority. Using  min-max normalization the intimal dynamic thresh­ old is obtained and based on threshold virtual machines
are mapped with tasks. Though the presented model is  simple, compared to the solutions of optimization-based  workflow scheduling the performance lags in make span  and resource utilization. Gravitational search algorithm  presented in [15] considers schedule length and cost ratio  for the optimization problem and obtains solution using  the gravitational search algorithm by minimizing the  cost and schedule length better than HEFT and genetic  algorithms.
The improved Firefly Optimization-based workflow  scheduling presented in [16] incorporates genetic algo­ rithm operators and quasi reflection learning procedures  to enhance the scheduling performances. The objec­ tive was considered to reduce the make span and cost  and it was attained better than traditional firefly and  other optimization algorithms. The Self Adaptive Fruit  Fly Optimization (SAFFO)-based workflow scheduling  presented in [17] considered cost and make span for the  objective function and obtained global solution through  the optimization model. The experimentation results  report that the presented model effectively reduces the  cost and make span over traditional GA, ABC and FFO  algorithms.
The optimized workflow scheduling model presented  in [18] utilizes Ant Colony Optimization to reduce the  cost and make span. The presented model initially utilizes  heterogeneous earliest end time for initial scheduling and  then utilizes optimization algorithm for optimal schedul­ ing of workflow tasks to physical machines. Experimental  results show that ACO based scheduling is better than  conventional scheduling procedures. The two-tier work­ flow model presented in [19] includes linear optimization  and gradient decent search-based resource estimation  and cluster-based resource scheduling for heterogeneous  cloud computing. The objective function considers cost  and execution time metrics. The presented optimized  scheduling and resource estimation effectively reduces  the workflow complexity in comparison to PSO.
The swarm intelligence PSO based workflow schedul­ ing model presented in [20] considers cost, energy con­ sumption and makespan in its objective function. The  optimization model converged with non-dominated  solutions which provide better exploitation and explora­ tion. Simulation results present the better convergence  and performances of optimization model with reduced  energy consumption and cost. Considering the cost and  make span in their objective function an immune PSO  based workflow scheduling is presented in [21]. The pre­ sented model overcomes the traditional PSO slow con­ vergence and provides enhanced speed and quality for  the scheduling process.

The DHJS algo­ rithm decreases the average waiting time by up to 30%  compared to other scheduling algorithms. Merits of this  approach include increased efficiency in resource allo­ cation, scalability for complex workloads, and reduced  processing delays. However, limitations include potential  complexity in real-time implementation and the require­ ment for extensive computational resources in scenarios  with rapidly fluctuating workloads.
A hybrid workflow scheduling algorithm combin­ ing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated  Annealing (SA) is proposed in [31] for energy-efficient  and deadline-aware task scheduling in fog and cloud  environments. The technique optimizes task prioritiza­ tion using PSO and improves task allocation using SA.  Key evaluation metrics include energy consumption and  makespan. The results show that the PSO-SA algorithm  enhances energy efficiency by 5% and reduces makespan  by 9% on average compared to the IKH-EFT baseline.  Other metrics, such as the percentage of IoT tasks meet­ ing deadlines, were improved by around 99%. The pri­ mary merits of the work include its ability to efficiently  manage resources, reduce energy consumption, and  improve task scheduling to meet deadlines and priori­ ties in a fog-cloud environment. However, the algorithm’s  complexity could be a limitation, especially when scaling  up in large, dynamic fog environments, potentially lead­ ing to increased computational overhead.

The reviewed workflow scheduling strategies exhibit  several strengths and limitations. Single metaheuristic  algorithms such as PSO, ACO, and GA are computation­ ally efficient and relatively simple to implement. They  are effective for basic task-to-resource mapping and can  optimize individual objectives like cost or makespan.  However, they often suffer from premature convergence,
lack robustness in high-dimensional search spaces, and  typically ignore critical QoS parameters such as energy  consumption and resource utilization. Hybrid models,  including PSO-GWO, ALO-GA, and HCRO, improve  global search and convergence rates by integrating com­ plementary algorithms. These methods generally perform  better across multiple objectives and exhibit improved  accuracy and load balancing. Yet, they tend to be com­ putationally complex, parameter-sensitive, and often lack  adaptability to dynamic or real-time cloud environments.  Additionally, many models are tailored for specific work­ loads or simulation settings, which raises concerns about  scalability and generalizability in real-world deployment.  These limitations collectively motivate the need for a  more balanced, adaptive, and comprehensive approach  like the proposed DSSSO model.

While numerous optimization-based workflow sched­ uling models have been proposed, most of them primarily  focus on minimizing makespan and cost, often neglect­ ing equally critical parameters such as energy consump­ tion and resource utilization. For instance, approaches  based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Genetic  Algorithms (GA), and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO)  demonstrate efficiency in reducing execution time and  cost but fail to comprehensively address energy-aware  scheduling requirements. Proposed work Cloud workflow scheduling environment Workflows are used to model scientific applications and  it requires high performance computing environment.  Generally, workflows are modeled as set of intercon­ nected tasks with more data or computing dependencies.  A cloud workflow management system in cloud executes  this workflow application. This management system has  the responsibility to manage, schedule and execute the  workflows based on SLA and user-specified QoS require­ ments. In the workflow engine, the data management  component performs data storage and movement as per  requirement. While executing workflow resource provi­ sioning and scheduling are considered important stages.  The resources required to execute the task are selected  and provided in the resource provisioning stage and  while scheduling the tasks are mapped into the best avail­ able resources.
The proposed high-level architecture given in Fig. 1 has  the workflow management system and it utilizes cloud  resource while executing the scientific workflow appli­ cation. The elements in the architecture are workflow  engine, workflow planner, workflow scheduler and clus­ tering engine. The proposed multi-objective hybrid opti­ mization algorithm is used in the workflow planner so  that suitable cloud service providers can be identified to  the users and data center loads can be tracked while allo­ cating resources so that the necessary quality of service  can be maintained. The proposed hybrid optimization- based workflow scheduling model includes metaheuristic  dolphin swarm and sparrow search optimization algo­ rithms. The proposed hybrid Dolphin Swarm Sparrow  Search Optimization (DSSSO) was obtained to effec­ tively solve the multi-objective cloud workflow schedul­ ing problem. Dolphin Swarm Optimization (DSO) was  selected for its robust exploration abilities. The dolphins’  echolocation and cooperative hunting behaviors of DSO

Cloud service providers have data centers in different  geographical locations and provide their services to users  through the internet without violating the service level  agreement. The data centers will have virtual machines  and it is considered as a computing resource. Each virtual  machine has different characteristics and different com­ puting features. Memory capacity, network bandwidth,
processing cores and cycle times will be different for  each virtual machine. The SLA specified either by user or  service provider provides the details of service and QoS  parameters. Violating the expectations will cause pen­ alty for both parties. Multi-task applications should run  smoothly on virtual machines and it is defined based on  the number of cores required to process the user tasks. In  the proposed model mathematical formulation, a set of  interdependent tasks of workflow application are consid­ ered. The tasks need to be executed with correct sequen­ tial order on a heterogenous virtual machines. By using  direct acyclic graph, the workflow application is modeled.  Consider if there are N virtual machines then it is repre­ sented as Npm = npm1, npm2, npm3, . . . npmn. The tasks  are represented as tuple tj = {m, j, pe} which provides  the details like identifier (j), length of identifier (m) in  million instruction and number of processors (pe) run­ ning for task on virtual machine.

Brief workflow is depicted in Fig. 5.  In the proposed DSSSO-based workflow schedul­ ing model, task-to-node assignment is handled through  a two-phase optimization process involving Dolphin  Swarm Optimization (DSO) for global exploration and  Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) for local refinement.  Initially, the entire workflow is modeled as a Directed  Acyclic Graph (DAG), where each node represents a task  and edges denote data dependencies. The cloud envi­ ronment is represented as a set of heterogeneous vir­ tual machines (VMs), each with specific computational  capabilities. The DSO phase generates a population of  potential scheduling solutions, where each individual  represents a complete mapping of tasks to VMs. Dur­ ing this phase, the fitness of each solution is evaluated  based on a multi-objective function considering makes­ pan, energy consumption, cost, and resource utiliza­ tion. Solutions are refined through echolocation-based  position updates and cooperative swarm behaviors. The  best-performing solutions are passed to the SSA phase,  which focuses on enhancing local exploitation. Here, task  assignments are further fine-tuned based on dynamic  safety thresholds and predator-avoidance behaviors,  ensuring high-quality VM allocations. Tasks are assigned  to VMs not only based on availability and execution  time but also considering QoS constraints like minimal  idle time, optimal power usage, and resource saturation

In the proposed hybrid Dolphin Swarm Sparrow Search  Optimization (DSSSO) algorithm the convergence occurs  in distinct phases. Initially, the global convergence begins  during the DSO phase, where dolphins explore a wide  range of solutions across the solution space. This explo­ ration ensures that the algorithm does not prematurely  focus on local optima and explores diverse regions of the  solution space. The convergence toward global optima  occurs when the dolphins, through echolocation and  cooperative hunting strategies begin to cluster around  the most promising areas of the solution space. This  happens as the DSO phase progresses, and more dol­ phins move toward higher-quality solutions based on the  multi-objective fitness function. The global convergence  primarily takes place in the early to mid-stages of the  optimization process when the algorithm has sufficient  diversity in the solution pool to explore the global search  space effectively.
The local convergence follows in the SSA phase, which  builds on the globally optimal regions identified by the  DSO. During this phase, sparrows refine the solutions  further by focusing on exploitation. They adjust their  positions based on the best solutions found by the DSO

Despite the demonstrated performance of the DSSSO  algorithm in simulation environments, its real-world  deployment presents several practical challenges. Firstly,  the computational complexity of the hybrid algorithm is  significantly higher than that of single optimization tech­ niques, due to the dual-phase nature involving both dol­ phin swarm behaviors and sparrow dynamics. Statistical analysis To further validate the superiority of the proposed  DSSSO model over competing algorithms, a statisti­ cal analysis was conducted on the experimental results  obtained from multiple independent simulation runs.  Each workflow experiment was executed 30 times  to account for the stochastic nature of metaheuristic  algorithms.
A one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) test was  initially performed to determine whether there were  statistically significant differences among the means of  the compared algorithms (Hybrid Bat Optimization,  Improved Bat Optimization, and DSSSO) across key per­ formance metrics such as makespan, energy consump­ tion, cost, and resource utilization. The ANOVA results  confirmed significant differences at a 95% confidence  level (p < 0.05) for all metrics.
To further strengthen the analysis, pairwise compari­ sons between DSSSO and each baseline method were  carried out using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, which  does not assume normal distribution of data. The results  showed that DSSSO consistently achieved significantly  better performance, with p-values below 0.01 in nearly  all cases. For example, the makespan improvements  of DSSSO over IBO and HBO recorded p = 0.008 and  p = 0.004, respectively, indicating strong evidence against  the null hypothesis of equal performance.
In addition, the mean and standard deviation of results  over 30 runs were reported for each metric. DSSSO dem­ onstrated not only superior average performance, but  also lower variance compared to baseline algorithms,  highlighting its robustness and stability. For instance, in  the Montage workflow, DSSSO reduced makespan vari­ ance by nearly 20% relative to IBO.
These statistical findings validate that the improve­ ments achieved by DSSSO are not due to random chance  but are statistically significant and repeatable across dif­ ferent workflows and experimental conditions.
Discussion The superior performance of the proposed DSSSO model  can be attributed to its effective balance between explo­ ration and exploitation during the optimization process.  The Dolphin Swarm Optimization phase provides strong  global exploration by simulating cooperative foraging  and wide-area search, which prevents premature con­ vergence and ensures diverse candidate solutions in the
early iterations. This global search capability is crucial  for handling the high-dimensional and complex search  space of workflow scheduling, where task-to-resource  mappings can easily lead to local optima. On the other  hand, the Sparrow Search Algorithm phase refines the  search through adaptive role-based behaviors that inten­ sify exploitation around promising regions, allowing the  algorithm to fine-tune resource allocation with higher  precision. The seamless integration of these two phases  enables DSSSO to dynamically transition from explora­ tion to exploitation, maintaining diversity while progres­ sively improving solution quality. This balance directly  contributes to the observed improvements in makespan,  energy efficiency, and cost reduction, as the algorithm  is both capable of identifying high-quality global solu­ tions and ensuring their stability through precise local  optimization.
Conclusion A hybrid optimization algorithm for optimal scheduling  of workflow task is presented using Dolphin Swarm (DS)  and Sparrow Search Optimization (SSO) algorithm as a  hybrid model (HDSSSO). The proposed hybrid optimi­ zation algorithm DSSSO effectively addresses the chal­ lenges of multi-objective cloud workflow scheduling. The  features of dolphin swarm optimization are incorporated  with sparrow search optimization algorithm to obtain  balance between exploration and exploitation, prevent­ ing premature convergence and refining solutions. The  hybrid optimization-based scheduling performance is  evaluated through simulation analysis considering bench­ mark workloads like cybershake, montage, epigenomics  and Ligo. The performances are evaluated using resource  utilization, cost, energy consumption and make span.  Results present the superior performance of proposed  scheduling model in terms of minimum energy consump­ tion, cost, and make span and maximum resource utiliza­ tion compared to existing hybrid bat optimization and  improved bat optimization algorithm-based scheduling  approaches. One of the minor limitations of the proposed  model is its increased computational complexity while  handling large-scale workflows. Also, the combination  of Dolphin Swarm and Sparrow Search algorithms may  lead to higher resource consumption compared to exiting  optimization algorithms. In the future, this research work  can be extended using learning algorithms to schedule  the workflows for improved resource utilization.
